scope: Prior visual semantic review notes for cached contact sheets and ambiguous-row details. Positions 1–192 retain their curated overlay pairs and source-pair notes. Positions 193–302 use the separately supplied read-only review, persisted in exercise-review-policy.json. This pipeline continuation did not re-review all images. Not biomechanical, clinical or coaching validation.

sheets.note: Press pairs distinguish lowered and extended arms. Cable fly uses open/closed arms; pec-deck does not. Bench phases are not inferred from source frame numbering.
Raises and rows have visible low/high or reach/pull pairs. Arnold rotation is absent. Romanian deadlift runs upright-to-hinge, unlike the conventional deadlift pair.
Rows show reach/pull; chin-ups and pull-ups show hanging/raised poses. Wide lat pull goes behind the head and remains blocked.
Squats, knee machines and thrusts have discernible bent/extended positions. Hack machine changes support geometry. Step-up requires detail review; only foot placement is visible.
Bridge, hip hinge, calf raises and curls have distinct positions. Wrist curl instead moves the elbow and remains blocked.

Dips and triceps extension phases are distinguishable. Planks use posture references. Cable crunch and ab-wheel mix incompatible setups. Treadmill and bicycle images are cycle examples, not starts/finishes.
Rowing and stair images are cycle examples. Fly uses frame 2 to show the open position; frame 3 bends elbows like a press. Bench/shoulder presses show lowered and elevated loads.
Raises use low/high arms. Pendlay lacks floor reset; neutral-grip pull-up lacks parallel handles. Single-arm cable row requires detailed reach/handle inspection.
Rack pull lacks elevated supports; belt attachment is unclear. Squats, deadlifts, Nordic and single-leg hinge show distinct positions. No precise joint angles are inferred.
Lunges show standing/lowered positions. Floor and bench-supported bridges are distinguished; barbell bridge instead shows a bench. Hinge pairs keep original drawing geometry.
Cable hip extension and abduction are readable. Machine kickback depicts a cable, and adduction does not show an inward crossing. Elevated-foot split squat keeps its platform.
Deficit lunge selects frame 2 rather than frame 1, which elevates the wrong support for this instruction. Back-extension variants and donkey calf source do not supply consistent intended setups.
Curls and triceps pairs show elbow-position changes. Spider curl lacks chest support. Two-dumbbell skull-crusher depicts one shared load and remains blocked.
Wrist extension moves elbows; unweighted Russian twist carries a load. Bird-dog uses quadruped frame 2. Mountain-climber and Pallof ordering need detail review; not every frame 3 is a reset.
Hanging knee raises and trunk movements have contrasting positions. Pallof hold is static, not a repetition. Swimming depicts a bench apparatus. Elliptical/rope/bike use representative cycle phases.

Hiking depicts an elliptical. Ski erg uses frame 2 for lowered handles. Push-up variants show distinct arm positions; archer uses central frame 2 and one side rather than implying both sides in two pictures.
Hindu push-up shows two phases of a longer sequence. Shoulder-tap combo lacks its push-up. Wall and inverted push-ups preserve support type; towel row lacks an anchor.
Prone T uses weights/bench rather than unweighted floor. Superman/holds and hangs use explicit static-reference labels. Negative pull-up correctly descends from frame 3 to 1. Commando grip is absent.

Shrimp selects frame 2 rather than the straight-forward free leg of frame 1. Skater squat mixes bilateral and lateral movements. Supported pistols, lunges and box/step variants retain their distinct supports.

Bridge march reverses drawing orientation between 1 and 3, so it is not proof of opposite legs. Frog bridge shows low/high hips. Clamshell changes knee bend; hamstring walkout uses straps and towel curl depicts stretching.
Ball curl changes body orientation. Banded frog/clamshell poses do not form consistent intended pairs. Remaining banded poses retain visible bands, anchors and recognizable direction of motion.
Band pull, row, diagonal rotation and dead-bug positions are recognizable. Hollow hold swaps variants, so blocked. Hollow rock/flutters are cycle examples rather than start/end positions.

Toe-touch stands instead of the specified supine movement. Seated knee tuck hangs on elevated supports. Plank-jack and bear-plank require larger review. Inchworm avoids composite frame 1 and selects separate views 2/3.

Copenhagen uses support/posture references; dragon flag shows lowering. Burpee omits intermediate phases in a two-picture summary. Half-burpee/squat-thrust need detailed leg review. Seal-jack depicts a support hold.

Cat-cow, circles and leg swings use cycle labels. Torso twist is weighted/seated and blocked. Static stretches use posture references, not fabricated repetitions; forward fold avoids the extreme first frame after review.
Wall calf images show static stance references, not a temporal sequence. Butterfly uses upright and gently inclined poses 1/2 instead of the deeply folded third pose.

bench-press.note: Frame 3 is lowered; frame 1 is the pressed position.

romanian-deadlift.note: Frame 1 is upright; frame 3 shows the hinge.

step-up.note: 512 px detail: frame 3 stands behind bench; 1/2 only place a foot. No completed ascent available; block the pair.

dumbbell-fly.note: Frame 2 retains the opening arc; frame 3 resembles a bent-elbow press.

incline-cable-fly.note: Select open frame 2 and closed frame 1; do not use press-like frame 3.

single-arm-cable-row.note: 512 px detail: working elbow remains flexed in 1/3; frame 2 adds another handle. No coherent reach-to-pull pair.

deficit-reverse-lunge.note: Frame 2 retains the forward foot on the platform; frame 1 depicts a different support arrangement.

mountain-climber.note: 512 px detail: 1/3 both advance the same visible knee. Use frame 2 plank and frame 1 knee drive; no complete alternating cycle claimed.

half-kneeling-pallof-press.note: 512 px detail confirms 3 is nearer chest and 1 farther forward; reverse prior overlay order.

plank.note: Frame 3 is supported on knees; frame 1 holds the extended-body posture.

side-plank.note: Both are lateral-support references; do not interpret minor hip-height differences as repetitions.

wall-sit.note: Frame 3 stands at wall; frame 1 shows the lowered hold.

cable-pallof-hold.note: 512 px detail: both already have arms forward. These are static references, not setup versus extension or a full rep.

superman-hold.note: Frame 3 rests on floor; frame 1 shows the held raised posture.

dead-hang.note: 512 px detail: all frames already hang; choose 1/2, avoiding the more laterally displaced third. Neither depicts mounting the bar.

active-hang.note: Both show straight arms. The pair does not demonstrate muscle activation or a repetition; activation is an instruction, not a visible finding.

negative-pull-up.note: Frame 3 is top and frame 1 is bottom. Retain 3→1; the source ordering differs from regular pull-up.

shrimp-squat.note: Use 3/2; frame 1 puts the free leg forward like a pistol rather than behind.

glute-bridge-march.note: 512 px detail: 1/3 reverse the entire drawing. Use 2→1 for base and knee lift, not a purported alternating-leg pair.

banded-donkey-kick.note: 512 px detail confirms visible band between legs and distinct down/raised bent-knee positions in 3/1.

banded-dead-bug.note: Frame 2 provides the flexed-leg reference, frame 1 extends one leg with band visible.

plank-jack.note: 512 px detail: frame 1/2 advance one knee rather than laterally open both legs. Block rather than relabel as a jump.

bear-plank.note: 512 px detail: frame 1 extends one leg; 2/3 do not provide a clear setup/hold pair for symmetric knees-under-hips posture. Block conservatively.

inchworm.note: Use separate frames 2/3; frame 1 combines two figures in one image.

l-sit-hold.note: Frame 3 is tucked; frame 1 extends legs. These illustrate entry to the hold, not repetitions.

copenhagen-plank.note: Frames 2/1 show bench-supported leg and lateral trunk position; no repeated up/down action is implied.

half-burpee.note: 512 px detail confirms no full extended plank: one knee remains forward in frame 1. No coherent full pair.

squat-thrust.note: 512 px detail shows asymmetry in extended-leg view and tucked legs elsewhere; no bilateral plank endpoint.

arm-circles.note: 512 px detail: frame 1 contains the only explicit circle arrows; select it with 3, not two arm elevations without direction.

labels: Apoyo de brazos en el marco
doorway-chest-stretch.note: Frame 3 shows the upright support; frame 1 advances the body between supports.

childs-pose.note: Frame 3 is quadruped; frame 1 folds hips toward heels.

kneeling-hip-flexor-stretch.note: Both show a half-kneeling stance; minor position differences are not claimed as a repetition or prescribed range.

hamstring-stretch.note: Frame 3 is upright; frame 1 inclines over elevated leg. Support height is not a universal prescription.

standing-quad-stretch.note: Frame 3 stands; frame 1 holds one foot behind.

seated-forward-fold-stretch.note: Use 3/2; avoid the deeply collapsed head/trunk position in 1.

cross-body-shoulder-stretch.note: Frame 3 has lowered arms; frame 1 brings one arm across.

wall-calf-stretch.note: 512 px detail confirms essentially the same static stance in 3/1. Two references, not start/end or a claimed increase in range.

butterfly-stretch.note: Use 1/2 rather than the deeply folded third pose; no forced knee pressure.
